author: Kaitlin Keane
title: Father of 7-year-old Norwalk twins hurt in hit-run crash starts fundraiser for recovery - NewsBreak
text:
By Kaitlin Keane ,
1 days ago
A file photo of a Norwalk police vehicle. (Norwalk Police/Contributed Pho)
NORWALK — What started as a birthday celebration for a Norwalk father’s 7-year-old twin sons ended in a hit-and-run crash that left his children injured and traumatized.
“What should have been a day of celebration turned into something traumatic that none of us were prepared for,” Wes Moore said in an online fundraiser he created to support his sons’ recovery.
Moore said on the GoFundMe page that one of his sons sustained a broken leg while one son was “badly injured,” and “both of them are deeply shaken by what happened.”
“They keep asking if the accident was their fault, and now they are afraid to go outside or even ride in cars,” he said.
“To make things even harder, my sons’ health insurance was canceled without notice, leaving us facing medical costs at the worst possible time," Moore wrote in the fundraiser.
As of Wednesday morning, the GoFundMe page had raised more than $2,300 through 40 donors. All donations will go toward covering the boys’ medical bills, doctor visits, follow-up appointments, physical therapy and trauma therapy as well as helping their family keep up with living expenses, the online fundraiser said.
The Norwalk Police Department said in a news release that patrol officers responded to the area of Cross Street and Wilton Avenue on Oct. 20 for a reported motor vehicle accident involving two juvenile pedestrians. The initial report stated a black Mini Cooper struck two juveniles who were crossing the street and then fled the scene, police said. Both juveniles were transported to Norwalk Hospital with non-life-threatening injuries, police said.
Responding officers interviewed witnesses and reviewed surveillance footage from the surrounding area, police said in the news release. The vehicle involved in the crash was located a short time later, and the operator, identified as Joseph Campbell of Norwalk, subsequently turned himself in to police, Norwalk police said.
Campbell, 68, is charged with evading responsibility with serious physical injury; evading responsibility with physical injury; failure to obey traffic control signal; operating without a license; operating an unregistered motor vehicle; operating without minimum insurance; and misuse of registration plates.
